This course could be so much fun, all the high-profile sociology and philosophy texts and discussions around media studies featured in the syllabus as well as the general appeal of media texts, close readings of movies, etc., yet this appeal is ruined by Burcu Hoca, her disdain towards students, her hurry with the course, and her inability to communicate the materials. Firstly, any participation you make in the class must be the exact set of words, in the same order that Burcu Hoca expects one to say, if not, she will just interrupt you and repeat the same three words she reads from her slides as if she explains anything further or in more depth. Secondly, there are mind-blowing discussions and theories in the syllabus and you actually go over them in class yet Burcu Hoca tries her hardest to make them as shallow and trite as possible. Seriously, how can you go over Levi-Strauss, Todorov, Propp or anything related to narrative analysis, semiotics etc. in a heartbeat by reading two sentences in slides and repeating them over and over again everytime their names come up as if it is some sort of match the theory with the author game? This strips the course of all depth which is perhaps the most interesting part. Halfway through the semester she announces that she won't have -some- of the classes because she will be at some random conferences and tries to speedrun the curriculum.
